rationale: Excess hair growth is the effect seen with oral minoxidil before its topical use for hair loss.
MedDRA lower-level term for excess hair growth.
Lower-level term; includes excess growth.
Preferred term; includes excess growth.
Local excess hair growth where a product is applied.
Androgen-pattern hair growth in women; androgenic medicines worsen androgenetic hair loss, so this effect does not point to the goal.
Eyelash growth seen with prostaglandin-analogue eye drops before bimatoprost was studied for sparse eyelashes.
Thicker eyelashes, the same effect.
In prostaglandin-analogue labels this term describes longer, thicker or darker eyelashes; it can also mean other changes.
Loss of eyelashes is the opposite effect.
Erections were reported during the angina trials of sildenafil.
The same pro-erectile effect.
A prolonged erection is the extreme of a pro-erectile effect; it is also caused by alpha-1 blockade (trazodone, antipsychotics), a different mechanism.
Describes pain, not a pro-erectile effect.
Weight loss seen with topiramate in epilepsy before its study in obesity. Also caused by illness and toxicity (for example cancer medicines), which this term cannot separate.
Lower-level term of weight decreased.
Less appetite is a route to weight loss; it is also a sign of toxicity.
MedDRA lower-level term for loss of appetite (not anorexia nervosa).
Lower-level term of decreased appetite.
Lower-level term of decreased appetite.
Sleepiness as an unwanted effect points to a possible use for poor sleep.
The same effect.
Lower-level term of excessive sleepiness.
Delayed ejaculation as an unwanted effect points to a possible use for premature ejaculation.
Absence of sweating as an unwanted effect points to a possible use for excessive sweating.
Slower bowel movement as an unwanted effect points to a possible use for diarrhoea.
Looser stools as an unwanted effect point to a possible use for constipation.
Low blood pressure as an unwanted effect points to a blood-pressure-lowering action.
The same effect.
